issues.description: Parameter mismatch for messageOnRide(): the problem statement and the template Main.java expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() that returns a string like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and the concrete classes (Pig, Seal) implement messageOnRide with a String parameter. This causes a compile-time / conceptual mismatch: students implementing the interface as specified in the task will produce a different signature than the solution, and the template Main’s example call r.messageOnRide() (no argument) will not match the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either: (A) Update the solution to match the specification/template by changing Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to Rideable.messageOnRide() and adapt Pig and Seal implementations to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (no equipment), or (B) if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template Main.java to require and demonstrate messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust the expected return-string in the specification to include the equipment. Aligning all three (problem, template, solution) to the same signature will remove the confusion and compilation mismatch.
